renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: evidence_dot_plot
  title: Evidence per fusion and predicted effect
  description: |-
    Each dot is a candidate fusion in one predicted effect on the coding sequence: its colour is the log of the supporting reads (spanning pairs plus unique spanning reads) and its size the share of that support that comes from unique reads. It answers which fusions have the strongest read evidence.
    How to read: a large, dark dot is a fusion backed by many reads that are mostly unique. A small, pale dot rests on few reads or on multimapping ones and needs scrutiny. FusionCatcher gives no single cut-off that separates true from false fusions.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ndaniel/fusioncatcher/master/doc/manual.md
  kind: dot_plot
  config:
    gene_sort: mean
  roles:
    cluster: predicted_effect
    gene: fusion
    mean_expression: log_support
    frac_expressing: unique_fraction

- component: figure
  title: Supporting reads by predicted effect
  description: |-
    Each segment is a candidate fusion: its supporting reads, grouped by the predicted effect on the coding sequence and coloured by the method that found it. It answers which kinds of fusion have the most read support and which aligners agree.
    How to read: tall bars in the in-frame group are the candidates most likely to produce a fusion protein. The colour shows which aligners found each candidate, so check candidates found by one method in the table.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ndaniel/fusioncatcher/master/doc/manual.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: predicted_effect
    y: supporting_reads
    color: finding_method
    labels:
      predicted_effect: Predicted effect
      supporting_reads: Supporting reads
      finding_method: Finding method

- component: card
  title: Supporting reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of reads supporting a candidate fusion (spanning pairs plus unique spanning reads), with the spread in the box. It answers how strong the typical evidence is.
    How to read: a low median with a long upper whisker is the usual picture of many weak candidates and a few strong ones. Open the dot plot to see which fusions the whisker belongs to.
  column: supporting_reads
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Candidate fusions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct fusion gene pairs, with the number of breakpoint rows next to it, and the bars rank the predicted effects. It answers how many candidates there are and what they do to the coding sequence.
    How to read: more rows than distinct pairs means some fusions have several breakpoints. In-frame candidates are the ones that can make a fusion protein.
  column: fusion
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: predicted_effect
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fusions, by predicted effect
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Unique spanning reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of unique reads that map on a fusion junction, with the median and the largest per candidate next to it, and the ring splits it by the method that found the fusion. It answers how much junction evidence there is and which aligners contribute it.
    How to read: unique reads exclude PCR duplicates, so they are a conservative measure of evidence. A ring dominated by one method means the other methods found few candidates.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ndaniel/fusioncatcher/master/doc/manual.md
  column: spanning_unique_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: finding_method
  caption: unique spanning reads, by finding method

- component: card
  title: Annotation labels per fusion
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean count of annotation labels FusionCatcher attached to a fusion pair (known fusion, oncogene, a cancer study it appeared in), with the median and the maximum next to it, and the histogram shows their distribution. It answers how well documented the candidates are.
    How to read: a fusion with many labels is a known event. A fusion with none is a novel candidate and needs stronger evidence. Labels such as a healthy-sample label can also flag likely false positives, so read them in the table.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ndaniel/fusioncatcher/master/doc/manual.md
  column: n_annotations
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: annotation labels per fusion

- component: table
  title: Candidate fusion genes
  description: |-
    Each row is a candidate fusion breakpoint: both partner genes, the annotation labels, the read evidence, the breakpoints and the predicted effect. It answers which fusions to validate first.
    How to read: sort by supporting reads and read the labels, then click a row to filter the other tiles to that fusion.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: fusion
